newsitem.title: USA: HFS, CUC in merger pact.
newsitem.headline: HFS, CUC in merger pact.

text.p: CUC International Inc. and HFS Inc. said Tuesday they agreed to a merger that will create a consumer services company with annual sales of $4.3 billion in businesses ranging from real estate to computer software.

The combined company will unite HFS's Avis car rental unit, Coldwell Banker and Century 21 realtors, and Days Inn, Howard Johnson and Ramada hotels, with CUC's Shoppers Advantage and Travelers Advantage member services, Welcome Wagon, and Sierra On-line and Knowledge Adventure computer software, among other operations.

Under the agreement, each share of HFS will be exchanged for 2.4 shares of CUC, which, based on CUC's closing price of $26 on the New York Stock Exchange on Tuesday, makes each HFS share worth $62.40. HFS closed at $58.50, up $1.50, also on the NYSE.
With 181 million shares outstanding, the deal values HFS at $1.12 billion.

HFS Chairman and Chief Executive Henry Silverman will serve as president and chief executive of the new company, and CUC chairman and chief executive Walter Forbes will be chairman. The two will switch titles on Jan. 1, 2001.
HFS and CUC will share equal representation on the new board.
Both companies will maintain their respective operations and said they expect no job cuts as a result of the deal.

"By combining HFS's brands and our consumer reach of more than 100 million customers annually with CUC's direct marketing expertise, powerful club membership delivery system, and 68 million memberships worldwide, we will create tremendous new opportunities that are not available to either company on its own," Silverman said.
The deal follows by less than a month HFS's merger with PHH Corp., which provides outsourcing services in vehicle leasing and fleet management. HFS is based in Parsippany, N.J.
HFS bought Avis for $800 million last July and Value Rent-A-Car for $175 million in March.
CUC, based in Stamford, Conn., is best known for its member services businesses, which provide coupon books and at-home shopping services to about 64 million subscribers.
CUC also has made recent acquisitions. It bought Sierra On-Line and Davidson & Associates, computer software companies, last year for $2 billion.
HFS is also involved in Hilton Hotels Corp.'s battle for control of ITT Corp.
HFS made no reference to the Hilton-ITT matter, but Hilton said Tuesday's deal "did not appear" to alter HFS's role in the ITT bid.
Under terms of their agreement, if Hilton succeeds in acquiring ITT, Hilton would license the Sheraton name to HFS and HFS would operate ITT's hotels.
